item.title: Ethiopia-Related Sanctions - Inactive and Archived
item.description:
Ethiopia-Related Sanctions - Inactive and ArchivedMark.Samara2@t… Mon, 09/13/2021 - 16:33

The national emergency declared in Executive Order (E.O.) 14046 of September 17, 2021, "Imposing Sanctions on Certain Persons With Respect to the Humanitarian and Human Rights Crisis in Ethiopia," has expired.

Following the expiration of the national emergency declared in E.O. 14046, the Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has removed from the List of Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN List), persons designated pursuant to E.O. 14046 whose property had been blocked. In addition, OFAC has removed Frequently Asked Questions pertaining to this program from its website.

Hong Kong-Related SanctionsTiffany.Hyatt@… Thu, 07/30/2020 - 10:33

Hong Kong-Related Sanctions Program Changes

 

CHANGES TO OFAC'S HONG KONG-RELATED SANCTIONS PROGRAM AS OF JULY 14, 2026 

 

The national emergency declared in Executive Order (E.O.) 13936 of July 14, 2020, "The President's Executive Order on Hong Kong Normalization," has expired. The expiration of the national emergency declared in E.O. 13936 does not repeal or otherwise affect the Hong Kong Human Rights and Democracy Act of 2019 (HKHRDA) or the Hong Kong Autonomy Act (HKAA) of 2020. Those statutes remain in effect.

 

Following the expiration of the national emergency declared in E.O. 13936, OFAC has removed from the List of Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN List), persons designated pursuant to E.O. 13936 whose property had been blocked solely pursuant to the International Emergency Economic Powers Act. Persons that remain sanctioned pursuant to the HKAA have been added to OFAC's Non-SDN Menu-Based Sanctions List (NS-MBS List) and assets blocked prior to July 14, 2026, remain blocked.

 

In addition to the above changes to OFAC's sanctions lists, OFAC intends to publish an amendment to the Hong Kong-Related Sanctions Regulations, 31 CFR part 585, in a future Federal Register publication to reflect the expiration of the national emergency. 

 

In light of the expiration of the national emergency declared in E.O. 13936, OFAC is also reviewing relevant FAQs and guidance associated with our Hong-Kong-related sanctions program and will update this website in the near term.

item.title: Promoting Accountability for Assad and Regional Stabilization Sanctions (PAARSS)
item.description:
Promoting Accountability for Assad and Regional Stabilization Sanctions (PAARSS)Tiffany.Hyatt@… Fri, 02/28/2020 - 12:54

Sign up for Promoting Accountability for Assad and Regional Stabilization Sanctions e-mail updates.

CHANGES TO OFAC'S SYRIA SANCTIONS PROGRAM AS OF JUNE 30, 2025 and AUGUST 24, 2026

OFAC no longer maintains comprehensive sanctions on Syria or blocking sanctions on the Government of Syria.  

OFAC maintains list-based sanctions on former Syrian President Bashar al-Assad and his associates, human rights abusers, Captagon traffickers, persons linked to Syria's past proliferation activities, ISIS and Al-Qa'ida affiliates, and Iran and its proxies.  

More details about these updates can be found below.

The following sanctions authorities are in effect with respect to Syria:

  • Executive Order (E.O.) 14312, of June 30, 2025, amends E.O. 13894 and authorizes the imposition of sanctions on Bashar al-Assad and his associates, human rights abusers, Captagon drug traffickers, and certain other destabilizing regional actors. To implement these executive orders, OFAC amended the Syria-Related Sanctions Regulations, 31 CFR Part 569, to, among other things, change the heading to the Promoting Accountability for Assad and Regional Stabilization Sanctions Regulations (PAARSSR), effective September 25, 2025. Persons designated pursuant to the PAARSSR may be found on OFAC's List of Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN List). Separate authorities maintain list-based sanctions on other actors in Syria and the region, including those supporting terrorism, Iran and its proxies, and Syria's past proliferation activities.

The following sanctions authorities are no longer in effect with respect to Syria:

  • Effective July 1, 2025, E.O. 14312 revoked the following six Executive Orders that formed the foundation of the Syria sanctions program and terminated the national emergency underlying those Executive Orders: E.O. 13338 of May 11, 2004; E.O. 13399 of April 25, 2006; E.O. 13460 of February 13, 2008; E.O. 13572 of April 29, 2011; E.O. 13573 of May 18, 2011; and E.O. 13582 of August 17, 2011. To reflect this revocation of authorities, OFAC removed the Syrian Sanctions Regulations, 31 CFR part 542 (SySR) from the Code of Federal Regulations on August 25, 2025. U.S. persons are not broadly prohibited from engaging in transactions with respect to Syria or the Government of Syria that were previously prohibited solely by the SySR. In addition, following the revocation of the above six E.O.s, persons designated solely pursuant to the blocking authorities of those E.O.s were removed from OFAC's List of Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN List) and all property and interests in property blocked solely pursuant to the SySR or related to persons removed from the SDN List were unblocked.
  • On December 18, 2025, the Caesar Syria Civilian Protection Act of 2019 (Caesar Act) was repealed when President Trump signed into law the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2026.
  • The determination regarding Syria as a State Sponsor of Terrorism was rescinded on August 24, 2026. Accordingly, Syria is no longer subject to prohibitions under the Terrorism List Governments Sanctions Regulations, 31 CFR part 596 (TLGSR), or 22 USC 7205(a)(1). Hay'at Tahrir al-Sham was concurrently removed as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist organization from the SDN List.  
  • The revocation of the aforementioned sanctions authorities does not affect past, present, or future OFAC enforcement investigations or actions associated with any apparent violations of the SySR that occurred prior to July 1, 2025 or of the TLGSR prior to August 24, 2026.

  • Tri-Seal Advisory: Sanctions and Export Controls Relief for Syria (Updated on August 24, 2026 )
